title: Which statements about atomics are true?

choices.text: Many threads doing `atomicAdd` on the same global address serialize, which can make a kernel far slower than a reduction.
A shared-memory histogram per block, merged into global memory at the end, cuts global atomics to one per bin per block.
`atomicAdd` on floats gives the same bits on every run, because the hardware adds in thread order.
Atomics need a `__syncthreads()` after each call to be correct.
